messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple containers on node-42 (us-west-2a) are hitting CUDA OOMs and restarting. First OOM at 03:02:18 UTC. Error rate ~12% for the last 6m. Affected pool: paged-attn-kv-prod-3. Potential customer impact: yes (some gen requests failing with 500).

incident-bot: Logs excerpt:
```
[03:02:18] runtime: cudaRuntimeError: out of memory (device 0)
[03:02:18] runtime: container restart: exit_code=137
[03:03:01] allocator: paged-kv: free_fragments=0, active_pages=2143, resident=63.9GB
[03:03:01] cache: kv_resident_bytes=68590720000, kv_evictions=12
```

alice_oncall: Acknowledged. I'm picking this up. @ben_runtime can you confirm whether this is fragmentation creeping up vs a sudden allocation spike? Also adding a link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paged-attn-oom

ben_runtime: Looking at perf counters now. Early signal is fragmentation + slow leak from long-lived KV entries (some sessions with huge prompt prefixes). Not a single big alloc. Evidence: high resident memory but low new_alloc rates. pmap snapshot:
```
PID 12345: rss=64GB, anon_hugepages=0, dirty=0
Allocator buckets: many small holes, total_free=1.2GB but non-contiguous
KV slab: live_chunks=1.1M, stale_chunks=420k (not yet GC'd)
```
Mitigation plan (short):
- trigger manual kv-scrub on pool paged-attn-kv-prod-3
- lower KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD to 0.6 for that pool (currently 0.8)
- temporarily disable paged attention for the hottest route and route to non-paged variant
- if still noisy, cordon node-42 and drain traffic to us-west-2b pool

carla_sre: Running scrub now (will post progress). Command I'm using:
```bash
# run from ops jump
./infractl node exec node-42 -- sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kv-scrub --pool paged-attn-kv-prod-3 --max-iter 200
```
Starting scrub... ETA ~3m.

carla_sre: scrub update: iteration=60/200, reclaimed=4.6GB, resident now 59.3GB. Some containers still spiking CUDA mem after GC (~2x/sec).

ben_runtime: Good. Also reduce batch size on that pool to avoid transient peaks: set MAX_TOKENS_PER_BATCH=512 -> 256. Command to hot-change in the runtime: 
```json
{"pool":"paged-attn-kv-prod-3","runtime_patch":{"max_batch_tokens":256}}
```
Applying now.

alice_oncall: Applying runtime patch and lowering evict threshold. Deploy-bot: can you confirm config apply?

incident-bot: CONFIG PATCH APPLIED by alice_oncall at 03:08:12 UTC -> {pool:paged-attn-kv-prod-3, max_batch_tokens:256, KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD:0.6}

dan_support: Customer ops update: two customers reported 500s (cust-omega, cust-lumen). cust-omega opened a ticket saying "generation failed repeatedly, 5 attempts". I'm on a call with cust-omega; offering to failover them to dedicated capacity.

emma_prod: Recommend failover routing for high-value customers. We should also flip traffic to a non-paged variant for the next 30m while we stabilize. Can we push a canary route?

alice_oncall: Initiating canary routing: moving 10% of traffic from paged-attn-kv-prod-3 -> paged-attn-nopage-prod-1. Command:
```bash
./routingctl shift --from paged-attn-kv-prod-3 --to paged-attn-nopage-prod-1 --percent 10 --ttl 30m
```
Shift started.

carla_sre: scrub completed. Total reclaimed=7.9GB, resident=56.1GB. No further immediate restarts in last 2m. Node-42 still showing occasional CUDA OOM traces but much less frequent.

ben_runtime: Observed a reduction in tail latency and OOMs after batch reduction + scrub + routing. Still seeing some non-contiguous fragmentation; next step is to schedule nightly compaction for this pool and add a proactive eviction pressure job. Creating a short PR to add a background compactor and reduce default KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD.

dan_support: Noted. Cust-omega moved to dedicated and reports OK so far. Updating tickets and sending postmortem note.

alice_oncall: Summary: root cause = long-lived KV entries & allocator fragmentation -> slow resident creep -> CUDA OOMs on node-42. Live mitigations: manual kv-scrub, lower evict threshold, reduce batching, canary route to non-paged variant, failover for impacted customers.

alice_oncall: Handoff to night shift (@oncall-night). Please pick up further compaction work and monitor paged-attn-kv-prod-3 for 6 hours. I'll follow up with a short incident report. :white_check_mark:
